newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.
newsitem.headline: Australian Broadcasting Corp Morning Update.

text.p: DEVELOPMENTS IN HUNTER STRIKE EXPECTED
Mining company Rio Tinto is to meet with New South Wales State Rail's Freightcorp today about an Industrial Commission order to get trains into its Hunter Valley Number One mine.
The miners' union has warned if Rio Tinto does try again to have a train cross the picket-line, it will only provoke further conflict.
Union members at the mine are in their fifth week of strike action because of management plans to put them on individual contracts.
CFMEU delegates at Cessnock today meet to consider an enterprise bargaining document released by Rio Tinto, which aims to remove what the company described as restrictive work practices.
Mine Manager Allan Davies said with talks re-opening, the company is not giving immediate priority to the train issue.
Both sides see negotiations on the new document as an opportunity to step back from a national dispute in the coal industry.
OPPOSITION DEMANDS ANSWERS ABOUT GOLD SELL-OFF
The Federal Opposition has turned up the heat on the Government and Reserve Bank Governor Ian Macfarlane on the issue of gold asset sales.
Macfarlane will be asked to appear before the Senate Estimates Committee next month, to explain the sale of two-thirds of Australia's gold stocks.

Questions have been raised about the appropriateness of Reserve Bank Board member and WMC Ltd chairman Hugh Morgan being involved in board meetings, when the sales were being discussed. Yesterday, both the Governor and Morgan released statements, which denied any wrongdoing through any potential conflict of interest.
But Shadow Assistant Treasurer Nick Sherry said there are other issues.

"We think it's appropriate that the Senate have an opportunity to question the underlying economic rationale, the budgetary implications, because the gold sale's had a significant effect on Australia's gold industry, share prices and the world gold price," Sherry said.
WESTPAC LOSING HOME LOAN MARKET SHARE
Despite Australia having its lowest interest rates in 30 years, one major bank has suffered a fall in the amount of money it is lending to aspiring home-owners.
All 49 of Westpac Bank's rivals enjoyed owner-occupier lending levels which either increased, or remained the same during May, compared with April
Over the same period, Westpac's figures fell by more than $500 million, after also having fallen the month before.
Westpac's Noel Purcell said the reduction is due to the bank's use of a funding method called securitisation, which means many of their customers' loans are funded through a separate company.
But even when the securitised loans are considered, Westpac's loan levels still fell marginally in May.
NT "WELL AHEAD" IN SPACE BASE RACE
The Northern Territory Government said it is at least a year ahead of Queensland, in the race to build an Australian satellite launch centre.
The government said an environmental impact statement for one of two preferred sites in the Territory is finished.
Queensland Premier Rob Borbidge announced that negotiations to build a space base in his state are well advanced, with sites in central Queensland and Cape York under consideration.
Borbidge has appointed an ex-astronaut to oversee the billion dollar project.
But Northern Territory Industry Minister Eric Poole said proposals for a base near Darwin are much further advanced.
QLD AND TAS SLIP-UP ON PORN CONSENT AGE
The Eros Foundation claims Queensland and Tasmanian Attorneys-General rejected moves to raise the age of consent for acting in pornographic videos from 16 to 18 years.
Eros lobbyist, Robbie Swan, said the two are being toasted by Australia's X-rated video producers, because they voted against the introduction of a new non-violent erotica category.

Swan said the industry is overjoyed at that decision, but is concerned Denver Beanland and Ray Groom had rejected the industry's recommendation that the age of consent for porn actors be raised to 18 years.
Because censorship issues rely on a cooperative approach from all the states and territories, it only takes one dissenting voice for a proposal to be rejected.
BIGGEST ANTI-HANSON RALLY YET EXPECTED IN GEELONG
Police have kept their tactics secret ahead of what protest groups expect will be a big anti-Pauline Hanson vigil tonight at Geelong, west of Melbourne.
But it has been confirmed that Melbourne police reinforcements will go to the South Barwon Civic Centre, where organisers expect thousands of demonstrators.
Despite tickets being on sale for three weeks, there are still seats free for Miss Hanson's cocktail party, dinner and speech, with the speech just over half booked.
Tight security surrounds the arrival of the Independent Federal MP, and One Nation Party founder, in Melbourne this morning and security guards will be on-hand as she visits Geelong businesses.
